# RESEARCH EXPERIENCE

**PhD Candidate** \hfill Sept 2021 - Present

*Institute for the Oceans and Fisheries* University of British Columbia 

* My PhD dissertation explores the ecological and fishery consequences of growing pinniped populations on multispecies, multistock salmon fisheries. The research involved modeling the population dynamics of 27 stocks, from five species, of Fraser River salmon and steelhead (*Oncorhynchus spp.*) to compare ecological drivers of productivity declines; conducting retrospective policy analysis of historical fishery conditions; and surveying commercial salmon fishers to document operational interactions with pinnipeds.
- *Skills: Statistical modeling, Bayesian modeling, R programming, Git/GitHub, stakeholder engagement*

**Graduate Research Assistant** \hfill Jan 2024 - Present

*United States Army Corps of Engineers*  

- As a part-time research assistant I conduct statistical modeling, using Bayesian mark-recapture models in JAGS, zero-inflated binomial regressions, and generalized additive models, to determine Chinook salmon (*Oncorhynchus tshawytscha*) passage success and survival through dams in the Willamette River system in Oregon. 
- *Skills: Statistical modeling, Bayesian modeling, JAGS programming, data analysis, stakeholder engagement, R programming*

**Research Analyst** \hfill Feb 2026 - May 2026

*Pacific Salmon Commission*  Vancouver, B.C.

- During a three month contract I analyzed salmon monitoring data to statistically evaluate the use of a new monitoring method for salmon passage through Hells Gate, a narrow gorge which poses passage challenges for sockeye (*Oncorhynchus nerka*) and pink salmon (*Oncorhynchus gorbuscha*) migrating up the Fraser River to their spawning grounds.
- *Skills: Statistical modeling, R programming,  Git/GitHub*

\newpage

**Aquatic Biologist II** \hfill Jun 2025 - March 2026

*Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada* Vancouver, B.C.

- As a contract research biologist, I used empirical harbour seal diet data to construct spatial-temporal models of seal diet composition and compare these estimates to those produced by Ecopath with Ecospace ecosystem models, to statistically validate ecosystem model outputs and inform field sampling programs.
- *Skills: Spatio-temporal modeling, VAST, ecosystem modeling, EwE, bioenergetics modeling, TMB programming*

**M.S. Student** \hfill Sept 2018 - July 2020

*School of Marine Science and Policy* University of Delaware 

- My Master's research involved analyzing data from a state-run trawl survey using multivariate statistical methods to describe the fish and invertebrate community in Delaware Bay, identify physical drivers of community composition, and evaluate long-term changes in the community.
- *Skills: Fishery independent data analysis, multivariate statistics, timeseries analysis, R programming*

**Undergraduate Senior Honors Thesis** \hfill Sept 2014 - May 2015

*Department of Sociology* Colby College 

- My undergraduate honors thesis project involved conducting in-depth interviews with harvesters to understand social and community implications of the changing American lobster (*Homarus americanus*) population, and subsequent management, on the lobster fishing industry in Maine.
- *Skills: Sociological research, interview design, stakeholder engagement*

**Research Intern** \hfill June 2014 - Aug 2014

*CIEE Bonaire* Bonaire, Netherlands Antilles 

- I used SCUBA field sampling methods to catch invasive lionfish, *Pterois*, and dissect and analyze stomach contents, to explore the predatory impact lionfish have on juvenile fish in Bonaire.
- *Skills: SCUBA, stomach content analysis, field sampling*

**Research Intern** \hfill Jan 2013 - Feb 2013

*Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History* Washington D.C. 

- I curated, identified, and photographed over 50 species of *pteropoda* to catalog morphology for research of the genetics, morphology, and biogeographic information of pteropods to better understand ocean connectivity.
- *Skills: Curation, phylogeny, Geneious software, Image J software*

# PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

**Teaching Assistant** \hfill Sept 2023 - Present

*Master of Data Science Program* University of British Columbia 

- For three years, I have been a part-time teaching assistant for several MDS statistics and computation courses. I lead coding labs, evaluate student work, and provide feedback. The courses included, *Programming for Data Manipulation* (DSCI 523), *Statistical Inference and Computation I* (DSCI 552), *Regression I* (DSCI 561), *Regression II* (DSCI 562), *Statistical Inference and Computation II* (DSCI 553), *Experimentation and Causal Inference* (DSCI 554).

**Teaching Assistant** \hfill Spring 2026

*Ecosystem Modeling with EwE* University of British Columbia 

- As a teaching assistant for a graduate-level ecosystem modeling course (FISH 501), which taught the use of Ecopath with Ecosim (EwE) for marine ecosystem modeling, I delivered lectures and provided feedback to students on course projects. 

**Graduate Writing Consultant** \hfill Sept 2022 - April 2024

*Center for Writing and Scholarly Communication* University of British Columbia 

- As a writing consultant I provided written and in-person consultations to graduate and undergraduate students on written work including class assignments, manuscripts, and dissertations.

**NOAA Sea Grant John A. Knauss Marine Policy Fellow** \hfill Feb 2021 - Feb 2022

*National Stock Assessment Program* NOAA Fisheries 

- As a Knauss Fellow I supported the National Stock Assessment Program by organizing a technical community, developing the Fisheries Integrated Toolbox, assisting in coordination of a new national stock assessment modeling framework (FIMS), and facilitating regional communication, to advance the NOAA stock assessment enterprise. 

**Communications Committee Chair** \hfill Oct 2022 - June 2026

- **Committee Member** \hfill June 2015 - Oct 2022

*Association of Marine Laboratories of the Caribbean* 

- In this volunteer position I managed internal and external communication, and helped organize three biennial scientific conferences, for the AMLC, a nonprofit which connects marine laboratories, scientists, students, and stakeholders in the Wider Caribbean Region.

**North Pacific Groundfish Observer** \hfill June 2016 – Jan 2018 

*Saltwater Inc. / NOAA Fisheries* 

- As a fisheries observer I collected data on catch, bycatch, and fishing effort on board commercial Alaskan fishing vessels to be used by the National Marine Fisheries Service to monitor fish populations, set catch limits, and manage commercial Alaskan fisheries.
